narrative_passages.title: The dry path in the sea

summary_for_children: Surah Ta-Ha tells how Musa saw a fire in the night and was called by Allah, how as a baby he was placed in a chest on the river, how he and Harun went to Pharaoh with gentle words, and how Allah saved the believers through the sea.
world_title: Fire in the Valley of Tuwa
environment_concept: A fire glowing far across a dark valley (20:10), a pair of sandals left at the valley's edge (20:12, an adaptation), a chest in the reeds (20:39), a dry path between walls of water (20:77) and an empty camp (20:88). Musa and every person are never shown; no idol is pictured.
architecture_and_scenery: Dark desert valley with a single far-off fire, a reedy riverbank, a sandstone palace forecourt, a parted sea floor of wet sand, and a camp beneath bare hills.

palette.lighting: One warm firelight against a blue night, then hard desert sun
palette.atmosphere: Cold night wind, river reeds, sea spray

areas.name: The Distant Fire
areas.description: A single fire glowing far across the dark valley; the walk toward it begins the world.

areas.name: Valley of Tuwa
areas.description: A hushed valley floor: the player leaves their own sandals at the edge (adaptation).

areas.name: The River and the Chest
areas.description: A wooden chest drifting along reeds to the bank; no person is shown.

areas.name: Dry Path Through the Sea
areas.description: Walls of water either side of a dry seabed path.

areas.name: Camp of the Calf
areas.description: An empty camp where a golden calf statue stands, later shown melted and scattered.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: Musa and the Mountain of Light
story_library.children_narration: While traveling with his family, Musa noticed a fire in the distance. When he approached, Allah called him and gave him a special mission. Musa was told to go to Pharaoh and invite him to turn away from wrongdoing. He asked Allah to help him and to allow his brother Harun to support him. The story continues through Pharaoh's court, the confrontation with the magicians, the escape of the Children of Israel, and the events that followed. Surah Ta-Ha also reminds us of Adam and the importance of following guidance.

world_idea.title: The Journey of Musa
world_idea.description: Explore a mountain landscape, an ancient Egyptian environment, and a sea-crossing observation sequence. Children investigate story clues and follow events without portraying or controlling Musa or Harun. ## Part 2 — Surahs 21–40

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Musa and Harun are never shown or played. The sea crossing is an observation from a distance, with no drowning.
